A work permit must be issued and qualified 
maintenance staff should carry the suitable safety category.
Safety fence (rope) with caution mark surrounding the work area is required.
Line isolation
Secondary injection test set
Ammeter, Voltmeter
Test lead

Make sure CT secondary 
 circuit are shorted at the incoming terminal blocks before isolating the relay 
 current circuit for test
Obtain copy of relay setting from field maintenance file

Connect test leads between the current terminals (40 and 41) on the relay 
 Fig(1)
Connect test leads between the voltage terminals (+1 and -2) on the relay.
Connect test leads between the time delayed contacts (11and 12) on the relay
Increase the current slowly until the contacts close
Record this value on the test sheet

Record the time response of relay where the time will stop once the relay has 
 picked up
Compare the recorded values with setting values

Repeat the above test steps for other phases by putting the current terminals 
 for phase S (50 and 51) and phase T (60 and 61)
Disconnect the test leads from the current terminals (40 and 41)
Disconnect the test leads from the voltage terminals (+1 and -2)
Disconnect the test leads from time delay contacts terminals (10 and 11).

Check that the CT and PT secondary connections return to its normal position 
 as before the test

If any equipment associated with the relay has been isolated it should be 
 returned to the service

Protection | Technical Procedure
Introduction
This document out lines the testing procedure 
P1, which must performed on an annually bases as indicated by Y1 in the above 
title block
The over current relays TMA 311,211,321,110 are quite suitable to protect the 
generator against over currents, short circuits and generally against faults 
between phase and earth
The first draft initiated by eng. Ayman Fathy Shita, tested by eng. Badawy Abd El-Alim, 
eng. Hassan Ali El-Sherbeny & eng.Ayman Fathy Shita at 22 October 2003, revised 
by EDEPCo. quality control eng. Adel El-Nagare, accepted by General Director eng. Hamed 
El-Sayed Mansour and approved by eng. Uosry Salama Head sector of Power 
Stations.
Safety Precautions
A work permit must be issued and qualified 
maintenance staff should carry the suitable safety category.
Safety fence (rope) with caution mark surrounding the work area is required.
Line isolation
Tools and Equipment
Secondary injection test set
Ammeter, Voltmeter
Test lead
Work to be Carried Out
Make sure CT secondary 
 circuit are shorted at the incoming terminal blocks before isolating the relay 
 current circuit for test
Obtain copy of relay setting from field maintenance file
Connect test leads between the current terminals (40 and 41) on the relay 
 Fig(1)
Connect test leads between the voltage terminals (+1 and -2) on the relay.
Connect test leads between the time delayed contacts (11and 12) on the relay
Increase the current slowly until the contacts close
Record this value on the test sheet
Record the time response of relay where the time will stop once the relay has 
 picked up
Compare the recorded values with setting values
Repeat the above test steps for other phases by putting the current terminals 
 for phase S (50 and 51) and phase T (60 and 61)
Disconnect the test leads from the current terminals (40 and 41)
Disconnect the test leads from the voltage terminals (+1 and -2)
Disconnect the test leads from time delay contacts terminals (10 and 11).
Check that the CT and PT secondary connections return to its normal position 
 as before the test
If any equipment associated with the relay has been isolated it should be 
 returned to the service
